title: Download With Care: Fitness Apps May Not Be Science-based
main_content:
You might want to do a little research on that fitness app you just downloaded.

It might look snappy and authoritative, but it’s possible there isn’t a bit of science to back up any of the claims it makes about getting you slim and fit, and that could be dangerous. Out of thousands of apps that promise to help you lose weight, only 17 were actually certified or developed by a health organization or university.

Clearly the world has a weight problem. The World Health Organization says 39 percent of us are overweight, and 13 percent are obese.

questions.question: What is the problem with some fitness apps?
options: They are too expensive for most users.
They often lack scientific support for their claims.
They are only available on certain devices.
They primarily focus on diet rather than exercise.
questions.answer: They often lack scientific support for their claims.

questions.question: What does the WHO report on the state of obesity?
options: Only 13 percent of the population is considered overweight.
39 percent of the population is overweight, and 13 percent is obese.
Obesity is not a significant health issue worldwide.
questions.answer: 39 percent of the population is overweight, and 13 percent is obese.

questions.question: What is the common idea about losing weight?
options: It requires a good fitness app for success.
It is solely dependent on exercise, neglecting diet.
There are many quick-fix solutions available.
It is primarily based on scientific methods.
questions.answer: There are many quick-fix solutions available.
